submissionAttempts.body:
Applicable host-contract version: **generation 1**.

Determination (local, authoritative-first):
1. Shipped pinned artifact is self-describing: node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/host.js declares `HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1`. `@ordarium/host-kit@1.3.1` re-exports that constant from core (dist/src/index.js), so host-kit introduces no second source.
2. `assertHostContract(v)` is exact-match and fail-closed (throws HostContractMismatchError otherwise), so the value the integration actually runs against is fixed by the shipped constant = 1.
3. Workspace code agrees: src/effects/runtime.ts assembles with `assertHostContract(1)`; test/host_conformance.test.ts CONF-A01 asserts assertHostContract(1) passes and assertHostContract(2) throws.
4. docs/engineering/13-host-adapter-conformance-spec.md names "contract generation 1".

Handling of the only apparent conflict (not a real one): docs (13-host-adapter-conformance-spec.md, 07-ordarium-alignment.md, docker/minimal/README.md) reference ordarium package version **1.2.0**, while package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml pin **1.3.1**. This is version-scoped/temporal documentation drift in the package version, not the contract generation: the upstream contract is bumped only when the host-facing port shape/semantics change (per core's own comment), and both the 1.2.0 and 1.3.1 lines ship HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1. docs/engineering/11-superseded-interface-note.md supplies the local precedence rule — the pinned dependency's shipped contract governs over the stale prose. So the sources are co-applicable to the same conclusion: 1.

No unresolved load-bearing conflict remains; local provenance (shipped artifact + precedence rule + matching code/test) is sufficient, so no peer escalation was needed.
